sections.h2: Hydrogen-based EU steel costs about 1.9 times ordinary hot-rolled coil

chart.title: Only a fully hydrogen-based plant pushes EU steel far above the market price
chart.sub: Operating cost, euro per tonne of steel.

sections.means: Where hydrogen is expensive, green steel costs far more than blast-furnace steel.
sections.todo: Judge green steel policy by the energy prices that make it expensive, not by the border charge alone.

sections.h2: Gas prices set the cost of direct-reduced iron, and Europe pays the most

chart.title: Gas alone costs a tonne of direct-reduced iron about €120 in Europe against €29 in the US
chart.sub: Gas per tonne of DRI (about 10 GJ), euro per tonne. Bases as labelled.
chart.source: This blog's arithmetic on TTF, India APM and Henry Hub prices.

sections.means: The gas that a direct-reduction plant burns costs more in Europe than in India or the US.
sections.todo: Lower European gas and power prices would do more for green steel than a higher price on imports.

sections.h2: With default CBAM values, imported coil costs more than EU-made coil

chart.title: CBAM on verified data closes most of the gap; default values reverse it
chart.sub: Hot-rolled coil, euro per tonne, early October 2026. CBAM for 2026 imports is paid in 2027; CIF excludes port and inland costs.
chart.source: Platts via EUROMETAL; Shanghai Metals Market; this blog's arithmetic.

sections.means: Imported coil is cheaper than EU coil before carbon costs, and the charge decides which side is dearer.
sections.todo: Allow verified plant data to count at the border so that a clean tonne is not priced as a dirty one.
